activities.topic: Introduction to Virtual Reality and Immersive Environments

activity_1.title: Close Your Eyes and Imagine
steps: Sit quietly and close your eyes for one minute.
Imagine yourself in a different place.
Think about what you see, hear, and feel around you.
Write 2–3 sentences describing your imagined place.

activity_2.title: Draw Your Virtual World
steps: Draw the place you imagined in your notebook.
Add elements like sky, land, water, or buildings.
Think about how your drawing represents a virtual world.
Relate your drawing to how VR creates environments.
examples: Mountain scene with clouds and sun
Ocean with fish and water waves

activity_3.title: Explore Your Surroundings
steps: Look around in all directions: left, right, up, down, and behind.
Observe how the view changes when you move your head.
Think about how your perspective changes.
Relate this to how VR works.

extra_exploration.task: Ask someone where they would like to travel using Virtual Reality and think about how VR enables exploration without physical movement.

think_and_notice: Which place did you imagine visiting?
How did your drawing show that place?
Why does VR make people feel like they are inside another world?
activities.discussion_instruction: Discuss your answers with your parents or elders.

learning_outcomes.title: Understand the concept of virtual environments
learning_outcomes.description: Students learn that Virtual Reality creates a world that feels real but is computer-generated.

learning_outcomes.title: Develop imagination and visualization skills
learning_outcomes.description: Students create and describe their own virtual environments.

learning_outcomes.title: Understand immersive experience
learning_outcomes.description: Students observe how perspective changes when they move their head.

learning_outcomes.title: Connect VR technology with real-life learning and exploration
learning_outcomes.description: Students understand how VR can help people explore places and experiences.

bonus_activity: Look at any picture in a book or poster.
Imagine stepping inside the picture and observing the surroundings.
Think about what you would see, hear, or feel.
Write one sentence describing that experience.
